decisive_items: an anti-centromere antibody level of 94.8 AU/ml
Raynaud’s phenomenon was elicited by cold‐water immersion of the hands
response.rationale: Anti-centromere antibody, Raynaud phenomenon, and pulmonary hypertension are highly characteristic of limited systemic sclerosis; polyarthritis can be an articular manifestation. RA is contradicted by negative rheumatoid arthritis serology, and SLE lacks anti-centromere specificity.

rejected.why: Rheumatoid arthritis serology was negative, and the anti-centromere antibody with Raynaud phenomenon and pulmonary hypertension point to systemic sclerosis rather than RA.

ANA is nonspecific, and anti-centromere antibody is not characteristic of SLE; the combination of Raynaud phenomenon, pulmonary hypertension, and anti-centromere antibody favors limited systemic sclerosis.
